evidence.reason: The inventory records only LoadState, ActiveState, UnitFileState, and FragmentPath for each declared unit. Systemd applies drop-ins from every unit-load directory, so a `crq-tick.timer.d` drop-in outside the declared local drop-in path can set `Unit=` to a different service while the local timer file and FragmentPath remain unchanged. The inventory can therefore report the timer as active and loaded even though it will not trigger the expected service, which is the configuration the release check should refuse before mutation. The existing `unexpected drop-in` check at lines 509-515 covers the declared local drop-in directory, not the effective drop-in set or trigger target.
